question.text: Unique Client Code (UCC) in derivatives trading is mandatory for:

answer.text: Every client must have a unique identification code mapped to their PAN, which must be used for all orders
Only institutional clients trading above Rs. 1 crore
Only for proprietary trades of the trading member
Only for trades in index derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: After KYC, each client is assigned a Unique Client Code (UCC) linked to the client's PAN. The trading member uploads the client's KYC details and UCC to the exchange or clearing corporation, and the trading account is activated once the UCC mapping is in place. Client orders carry the client account number to identify the client. The Trap: UCC is not limited by client type, order size, or product. It applies to every client across all derivative trades, not only institutional clients or index derivatives. Note: UCC is created post-KYC, mapped to PAN, and uploaded to the exchange or clearing corporation before trading is activated.
